dedupe_keys.name: dtcc platform open digital twin platform for cities

description: The DTCC Platform is an open-source environment for creating, simulating and visualising digital twins of cities, to support interactive and data-driven urban planning and design. It is developed by the Digital Twin Cities Centre at Chalmers University of Technology in Gothenburg as an open, multimodal data, modelling, simulation and visualisation environment, with interactive planning, design, exploration, experimentation and optimisation of urban spaces as its main use cases. The centre describes it as collaborative research within the centre, developed from 2022 onwards and released under the MIT licence; the project entry, dated 31 October 2025, names Anders Logg and Vasilis Naserentin as contacts. Other centre projects listed alongside include AI-based 3D city modelling, digital twins of construction sites and live buildings, digitising urban trees, and mixed reality for decision support. Coverage: generic; city models are built from the data a user loads. Access: open source. Licence: MIT. Caveats: the centre's JavaScript site and its platform documentation host could not be read in full here (the documentation host returned a gateway error), so modules, repositories and release versions were not confirmed. Simulation uses: city-scale 3D model generation and simulations for urban planning and design scenarios. Related records: CityJSON, the OGC CityGML standard and the City Energy Analyst.
